rationale: I designed a balanced initial candidate with 5 sensors spaced evenly across the front to detect the line well, using a medium sensor size (0.012 m) for good resolution and coverage. The wheel track and body width are set moderately wide (0.14 m and 0.14 m) to provide stability without risking off-track penalties. The wheel radius is 0.035 m for a good balance of speed and torque, and mass is set to 0.8 kg to keep inertia manageable. The controller uses moderate base speed (1.2) to encourage fast progress but avoid stalling, with PID gains tuned to moderate values (kp=8, ki=0.5, kd=3) to provide responsive but stable steering. Sensor weights are set to steer left or right based on sensor position, with stronger weights on outer sensors to detect line edges. The line loss strategy is 'last_direction' to continue searching in the last known direction, reducing stalls. I request a broad set of observations including completion, progress, errors, and line loss events to evaluate performance and guide future tuning. This candidate aims to complete the track reliably with good speed and minimal line loss, providing a solid baseline for iterative improvement.
